title: Only 6% Of Adults Can Pass This Police Officer Entrance Exam
summary: Explore observation and investigative judgement through clues, practical situations and fresh challenges.

landing.intro:
Listen closely. Think clearly.
Follow the facts.

about.body: Connect the facts, notice the details and test your understanding of observation and investigative judgement. Each checkpoint reveals your topic profile before a different challenge begins.

steps: Read the clues and choose one answer.
See your topic profile at each checkpoint and continue to a new challenge.
Reveal your overall result, then optionally review the answers you missed.

about.disclaimer: For entertainment and general learning only. This is not an official police recruitment, legal, fitness, medical, psychological or employment assessment. Laws and operational procedures vary by jurisdiction.

police-s1q1.question: At a reported incident, why first assess immediate dangers?

answers.a1: To establish guilt from the scene alone
answers.a3: To protect people and guide a safe response
answers.a4: To guarantee no assistance is needed

police-s1q2.question: Two witnesses are discussing their memories together. What risk should an investigator recognise?

answers.a4: Their accounts may influence one another

police-s1q3.question: Why record the condition and location of an item before moving it when appropriate?

answers.a1: To avoid identifying who handled it

police-s1q4.question: What does chain of custody document?

answers.a3: The handling and transfer of an item of evidence
answers.a4: The order of people in a public queue

police-s1q5.question: A person is distressed and struggling to follow questions. What can help?

answers.a1: Treating distress as proof of guilt
answers.a2: Calm, clear communication with suitable support
answers.a3: Adding threats to speed up the account

police-s1q6.question: Why avoid announcing an unverified claim as an established fact?

answers.a1: It can mislead people and prejudice the assessment
answers.a3: Only written claims can cause confusion
answers.a4: Confidence turns a claim into proof

police-s1q7.question: A report identifies a vehicle only by colour. What is the limitation?

answers.a1: Many vehicles may share that colour
answers.a2: No further detail can ever help
answers.a3: The report proves who was driving

police-s2q1.question: Which question invites a person to describe an event in their own words?

answers.a4: “It happened exactly as I said, correct?”

police-s2q2.question: Someone pauses while describing a difficult event. What is a useful response?

answers.a1: Allow time and offer a calm opportunity to continue
answers.a2: Ask several unrelated questions at once
answers.a3: Immediately fill in the missing details
answers.a4: Treat the pause as proof of dishonesty

answers.a1: Paying attention and checking your understanding
answers.a2: Planning your next speech while ignoring the answer
answers.a4: Speaking more loudly than the other person

police-s2q4.question: A term is unfamiliar to the listener. What helps?

answers.a3: Explain it using clear, familiar words

police-s2q5.question: Two people use the same word differently. What should be clarified?

answers.a1: Nothing; identical words always mean identical ideas
answers.a2: What each person means by the word

police-s2q6.question: Which response checks understanding without assuming agreement?

answers.a3: “There is no need to explain further”

police-s2q7.question: A language barrier affects an important discussion. What is the strongest support?

answers.a4: Using a child to translate sensitive details

police-s3q1.question: Two people give different times for the same event. What is the best next step?

answers.a1: Average the times and call that a fact
answers.a3: Choose the more confident speaker automatically
answers.a4: Check each account against other reliable information

police-s3q2.question: Which statement records an observation rather than an assumption about motive?

answers.a1: The person intended to mislead everyone
answers.a2: The person never cared about the meeting
answers.a3: The person left the room at 14:10
answers.a4: The person left because they were guilty

police-s3q3.question: A photograph has no known date or location. What should be checked before relying on it?

answers.a2: Whether it matches a preferred conclusion

police-s3q4.question: A claim is repeated by three websites, all quoting one unnamed source. What does that show?

answers.a2: Proof that no further checking is needed
answers.a3: Proof that the claim is accurate
answers.a4: Repeated reporting, not three independent confirmations

police-s3q5.question: All authorised visitors have a pass. Mira has a pass. What follows from that rule alone?

answers.a2: Mira cannot be an authorised visitor
answers.a3: Mira must be an authorised visitor
answers.a4: It does not prove Mira is an authorised visitor

police-s3q6.question: A new reliable fact contradicts your initial explanation. What is the sound response?

answers.a1: Change the fact to fit the explanation
answers.a3: Treat your first idea as unchangeable

police-s3q7.question: A report says an event happened after a change. Does that timing alone prove the change caused it?

answers.a2: Yes; if the report is long enough
answers.a4: No; earlier events can never cause later ones

police-s4q1.question: A decision affects a close friend. What should a professional recognise?

answers.a1: A reason to hide the relationship

police-s4q2.question: Which approach treats comparable cases fairly?

answers.a1: Use appearance as the only criterion
answers.a3: Apply relevant criteria consistently and consider relevant differences
answers.a4: Change criteria after seeing each person’s name

police-s4q3.question: A private record is useful for a task. What should determine access?

answers.a1: Whether the person is well known
answers.a3: Whether the file is easy to open
answers.a4: Authorised purpose and applicable access rules

police-s4q4.question: You discover an error in your own report. What supports accountability?

answers.a1: Leave it because nobody has noticed
answers.a2: Correct it transparently through the appropriate process

police-s4q5.question: What does informed agreement require in a meaningful discussion?

answers.a1: Relevant information and an opportunity to understand and choose
answers.a2: A promise that questions are forbidden
answers.a4: A decision made by an unrelated observer

police-s4q6.question: A gift could influence a professional decision. What is the appropriate response?

answers.a2: Hide the gift from the record
answers.a4: Follow the conflict-of-interest and gifts policy

police-s4q7.question: A rule applies to everyone in a process. A popular person asks for a private exception. What is appropriate?

answers.a2: Grant it without recording the reason
answers.a3: Change the rule only for that person without explanation
answers.a4: Use the authorised process for any exception

police-s5q1.question: Two records describe the same event but give different dates. What should be done?

answers.a3: Check the discrepancy against reliable original information
answers.a4: Average the dates and treat that as verified

police-s5q2.question: Which note separates a statement from a verified fact?

answers.a2: “Lee reports that the door was open; this has not yet been checked”
answers.a3: “No check is needed because the story is detailed”
answers.a4: “The door was certainly open because Lee said so”

answers.a1: To remove the need for dates
answers.a2: To make all information automatically true
answers.a3: So its source can be assessed and followed up
answers.a4: To prove every source is independent

police-s5q4.question: A document is a draft. What does that mean?

answers.a1: It may still change before being finalised
answers.a4: Every statement has been legally certified

police-s5q5.question: A file has been revised several times. What helps identify the current version?

answers.a1: Whichever copy is easiest to find
answers.a2: A clear version and approval record

police-s5q6.question: An entry is missing from a record. What does that establish by itself?

answers.a2: The information is not recorded there
answers.a3: The event definitely did not happen

police-s5q7.question: Why preserve an original record when making an authorised correction?

answers.a1: To guarantee the original was correct
answers.a2: To prevent anyone seeing the correction
answers.a3: To make the record harder to understand

police-s6q1.question: A log lists arrival at 08:42 and departure at 09:07. How long was the visit?

police-s6q2.question: A note says the person turned left while facing east. Which direction did they then face?

police-s6q3.question: A receipt is timed 14:10; a verified entry record is timed 14:35 on the same clock. Which happened first?

police-s6q4.question: There are 6 sealed bags, each containing 4 labelled items. How many items are listed?

police-s6q5.question: A location is 2 blocks north and then 1 block west of a starting point. In which general direction is it?

police-s6q6.question: A record describes a blue jacket and black bag. Which description changes only the bag?

police-s6q7.question: A camera clock is known to be 3 minutes slow. It displays 12:27. What is the actual time?

police-s7q1.question: A rule says: only members may enter. Sam is not a member. What follows under that rule?

answers.a1: Sam may enter if the queue is short
answers.a3: The rule says nothing about Sam

police-s7q2.question: Every approved application has a signature. This application has no signature. What follows?

answers.a2: It is not approved under the stated rule

police-s7q3.question: A service opens only on Monday, Wednesday and Friday. Which day is definitely excluded?

police-s7q4.question: Either Room A or Room B is booked, but not both. Room A is booked. What follows?

police-s7q5.question: A rule requires both a form and proof of identity. Only the form is present. What is missing?

answers.a1: A document not mentioned in the rule
answers.a3: A second copy of the form

police-s7q6.question: A policy says every urgent request is reviewed today. This request was reviewed today. What can you conclude?

answers.a1: It may or may not have been urgent

police-s7q7.question: Three meetings happen in order: Ana before Bo, and Bo before Cam. Who meets last?

police-s8q1.question: A supply box holds 24 items. Six are used. What fraction remains?

police-s8q2.question: A task begins at 14:35 and lasts 50 minutes. When does it finish?

police-s8q3.question: Four equal groups share 36 items. How many items are in each group?

police-s8q4.question: A reading rises from 40 to 50. What is the percentage increase?

police-s8q5.question: A plan uses a scale of 1 cm to 2 m. What distance does 6 cm represent?

police-s8q6.question: Three loads weigh 12 kg, 15 kg and 18 kg. What is their total mass?

police-s8q7.question: A checklist has 20 items. Four remain unchecked. What percentage is complete?

police-s9q1.question: A colleague suggests leaving out evidence that contradicts a theory. What supports a fair investigation?

answers.a1: Remove it to simplify the account
answers.a3: Preserve and report relevant evidence, including contradictions

police-s9q2.question: Why should questions avoid assuming facts that have not been established?

answers.a1: The wording can influence the answer

police-s9q3.question: A crowd gives conflicting descriptions. What is a useful next step?

answers.a1: Record accounts and check reliable independent details
answers.a2: Choose the most repeated story as proven
answers.a3: Assume every account is deliberately false

police-s9q4.question: Which detail is most useful in a factual incident description?

answers.a4: A conclusion based only on clothing

police-s9q5.question: Why should a person’s rights remain relevant during an investigation?

answers.a2: An allegation automatically removes all rights
answers.a3: Rights apply only after a case is solved
answers.a4: Investigative aims do not remove the duty to respect human dignity

police-s9q6.question: A decision must follow a specified procedure. What should uncertainty trigger?

answers.a2: A guess based on an unrelated case
answers.a3: Clarification through the appropriate authority or guidance

police-s9q7.question: What is an important purpose of recording reasons for a decision?

answers.a2: To allow the decision to be understood and reviewed
answers.a4: To guarantee the decision can never be questioned

police-s10q1.question: A plan sets a goal but no way to check it. What is missing?

police-s10q2.question: A decision is based on an old assessment, and circumstances have changed. What is needed?

answers.a1: A decision based on memory alone
answers.a2: Automatic repetition of the old decision

police-s10q3.question: What is a useful purpose of supervision or professional consultation?

answers.a1: To avoid responsibility for every action
answers.a2: To reflect on difficult decisions and improve practice
answers.a4: To guarantee nobody can make a mistake

police-s10q4.question: A task needs expertise you do not have. What is the appropriate response?

answers.a2: Seek suitable advice or referral within the process
answers.a3: Choose the fastest answer regardless of risk

police-s10q5.question: Two team members believe the other will make a follow-up call. What needs to be agreed?

answers.a3: Who is responsible and when the action is due
answers.a4: Only the title of the file

police-s10q6.question: A solution worked once. Does that guarantee it will fit every future case?

answers.a1: Yes; one success establishes a universal rule
answers.a2: No; successful ideas can never be reused
answers.a4: Yes; if the solution is easy to remember

police-s10q7.question: What makes feedback useful for improvement?

answers.a2: A claim that change is impossible
answers.a3: A personal insult with no example
answers.a4: Specific observations and a clear next step
